name: Bridgetown and the Careenage
tagline: The working capital around its inner harbour
description: The centre of the city around the Careenage, the narrow inlet where the schooners once tied up, with Parliament, the Chamberlain Bridge and the shops of Broad Street. It empties after the cruise ships leave and is more a place to do business than to live.
bestFor: Anyone who needs banks, government offices and the bus terminals daily
pros: Both island bus terminals are here
cons: Hot and short on shade at midday

name: Garrison Historic Area
tagline: The old military quarter with the racetrack in the middle
description: The UNESCO-listed garrison just south of the centre, built around the Savannah where horse racing still runs, with the Barbados Museum in a former military prison and Georgian barracks around the edge. It is walkable, green and quieter than the city.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting space and history within reach of the capital
pros: The Savannah for running and racing
Ten minutes to the centre on foot
cons: Few restaurants in the immediate area

name: Hastings and Rockley
tagline: The south coast strip with the boardwalk
description: A run of apartments, restaurants and small hotels along the south coast, joined by the Richard Haynes boardwalk that runs a kilometre and a half above the sand. It is the most practical place on the island to live without a car and where most long-stay visitors end up.
bestFor: Remote workers who want the beach and a bus route in the same place
pros: Buses to Bridgetown every few minutes
cons: Main road traffic behind the beachfront
Sargassum lands here in some years

name: St Lawrence Gap
description: A short curving street between two beaches holding most of the island's bars, clubs and late restaurants, busy every night of the week in season. It is the loudest address in Barbados and the reason people either book here deliberately or avoid it entirely.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is being able to walk home from a bar
pros: The island's nightlife on one street
Beaches at both ends of the Gap
Constant buses along the coast road

name: Holetown
tagline: The calm west coast, and the expensive one
description: The centre of the platinum coast, where the sea is flat, the sunsets face west and the villas cost what they cost. Holetown itself has a small centre with a supermarket and restaurants, and the first English settlers landed here in 1627.
bestFor: Anyone prioritising calm swimming water and willing to pay for it
pros: The calmest swimming on the island
Good restaurants and a proper supermarket
cons: The most expensive part of Barbados
